transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um... well, honestly, the thing that kind of scared me into coming in—and I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up here—is that my eating has just been... really all over the place lately. 

I mean, I don't want to make a huge deal out of it, but some days I just completely forget to eat my meals. And then other nights, well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but I'm just tearing through takeout and snacks way after midnight. I know it probably sounds a bit silly to come in just for that, but it's really not like me. Is that... does that make sense to bring up?
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Well, um, like I was just saying about how my eating has been so all over the place... I haven't actually stepped on a scale recently, to be honest. I guess I've been a little afraid to look. 

But with forgetting to eat entirely some days and then... you know, doing the whole midnight snack and takeout thing I mentioned... my clothes definitely feel like they're fitting a bit differently. I really try to keep myself looking put together for work, being in sales and all, so it's been bothering me a bit, even if it's not a huge difference. I hope it's not too bad. Does that... does that answer your question okay?
Do you find that your eating or not eating is related to how you're feeling at the time?

Um, well, I guess I haven't really thought about it like that. I mean, I try not to let my moods dictate things too much, you know? I want to stay professional and upbeat, especially for my job. 

I suppose maybe when I'm feeling really... energized, or just have a lot going on, that's when I might forget to eat. I just get so focused on doing things. And then maybe the late-night eating is when I'm just finally winding down? I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't think it's tied to feeling sad or anything bad like that, if that's what you mean. I try to keep a positive attitude. Does that make sense, or were you looking for something more specific?
Do you ever feel like you can't stop eating once you've started during those late-night episodes?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I completely lose control or anything like that. I really don't want to make it sound worse than it is, you know? I try to keep a good handle on things. 

I guess, like I was mentioning earlier, it's just that my routine is so all over the place right now. Because I'll go those whole days where I just completely forget my meals, by the time midnight rolls around and I'm finally eating, I just... I sort of overdo it with the takeout and snacks. But I can stop if I really need to, I promise. It's just that bouncing back and forth between not eating and then eating so much is what honestly scared me into making this appointment. I just want to get back to my normal, professional self. I hope that doesn't sound too terrible?
Do you usually feel guilty after those late-night episodes of eating a lot?

Um, guilty? Not exactly. I mean, I know eating a bunch of takeout at midnight isn't exactly the healthiest habit, especially for my waistline, but I try not to beat myself up over it. I really want to stay positive, you know? 

I usually just figure my body was finally catching up because I was so busy and missed lunch or dinner. So it's more just... frustration that my routine is off, rather than sitting there feeling terrible about myself. I always try to just wake up the next day and focus on doing better and being productive. Is that a normal way to look at it? I hope I'm making sense.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past few months?

Um, well, I haven't really been weighing myself, to be perfectly honest. I try not to obsess over the scale, you know? I want to keep a healthy mindset. 

But I guess... well, like I was saying before, the whole reason I even made this appointment—which honestly was a little scary for me to do—is just because my eating has been so all over the place lately. Going from completely forgetting to eat all day because I'm so focused, to just tearing through all that takeout and snacks after midnight... I'm sure my weight has probably fluctuated a bit because of that. My clothes fit a little differently depending on the week, but I wouldn't say it's anything drastic or out of control. I really am trying to keep it together. Does that answer your question okay?
Do you think your irregular eating patterns might be related to stress or how you're coping with pressure at work?

Um, stress? Well, I mean, work is definitely busy, but I wouldn't say I'm, like, overwhelmed or handling it badly. I really try to stay on top of things and keep a positive attitude, you know? I want to be a good employee. 

But I guess... well, like I've been saying, the whole eating thing is honestly what scared me into coming in to see you. It's just so back and forth. I don't think it's necessarily that I'm stressed, it's more just... getting caught up. Like, some days I'm just so dialed into what I'm doing that I completely forget meals altogether. And then, because of that, other nights I'm just tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight because I realize I haven't eaten. 

I'm really trying to get it under control, though. I don't want you to think I'm just completely falling apart or anything. I just want to get back on a normal schedule. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
Do you think you eat more at night as a way to deal with feelings or emotions from the day?

Um, dealing with feelings? No, I really don't think I'm an emotional eater or anything like that. I try to handle my emotions in a really healthy way, honestly. I don't want to use food as a crutch. 

But I guess... well, like I've mentioned a couple of times, the whole eating thing is honestly the main reason I got scared enough to come in here. It's just been so all over the place. It's not that I'm sad or upset at night, it's just... some days I completely forget to eat anything at all because I'm just so focused, and then, you know, other nights I'm tearing through all that takeout and snacks after midnight because my body is just starving. 

I'm really trying my best to fix it, though. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around eating my feelings every night. I just want to be healthy and get back on track. Is that a normal thing to happen when you're busy? I really hope I'm being helpful with these answers.
Do you usually eat at night because you feel hungry?

Um, well, yes, I think it's mostly just physical hunger. I mean, I try not to eat late at night because I know it's not the best habit, and I really do want to take good care of myself. 

But I guess... well, I know I sound like a broken record, but this whole eating thing is honestly what pushed me to make this appointment. It's just been so erratic. Like I was saying, it's not that I'm trying to binge or anything, it's just that some days I get so wrapped up in what I'm doing that I completely forget to eat a single meal. And then, naturally, by the time it's past midnight, my body is just so hungry that I end up tearing through whatever takeout or snacks I can find. 

I'm really trying to be more disciplined about it, though. I don't want you to think I'm just completely out of control with my habits. I just want to get back to a normal routine. Am I making sense? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you ever feel like you're eating at night because you can't stop yourself, even if you wanted to?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I can't stop myself. I really don't want you to think I have some kind of binge eating problem or that I'm totally out of control. I have a lot of willpower, usually, and I really try to make good choices. 

It's just... well, like I keep mentioning, because it really is the main reason I'm here... my eating is just so all over the place right now. It's not about a lack of control at night, it's just the consequence of the day, you know? Like I said, I'll go a whole day completely forgetting to eat because I'm just so dialed in, and then... yeah, after midnight I'm just starving and tearing through takeout and snacks. 

But I could stop if I wasn't so hungry, I promise. I'm really trying to get better at eating during the day so this doesn't happen. Does that sound like a reasonable explanation? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong impression about my habits.
Do you find that you are just not interested in eating during the day, which is why you end up eating more at night?

Um, yeah, I guess you could say that. It's not that I'm purposely avoiding food or trying to starve myself during the day, I just... I don't really have an appetite or even think about it when I'm working. I really do try to eat a good lunch when I remember, I promise. 

I know I keep saying the same thing, and I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself too much. But honestly, that's the exact thing that scared me into coming in to see you. My eating has just been so all over the place lately. It's exactly like you said—I completely forget meals during the day, and then the flip side is tearing through all those snacks and takeout after midnight because my body is just trying to catch up. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out. I'm really trying my best to give you good answers.
Do you feel like you're not eating during the day because you're intentionally skipping meals or because you're just not feeling hungry?

Um, well, it's definitely not intentional. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm trying to starve myself or do anything harmful like that. I know how important it is to keep a regular schedule, and I really do try to be responsible about my health. 

It's just that I honestly don't feel hungry during the day, or I just get so focused that it doesn't even cross my mind. I know I must sound like a broken record, and I'm really sorry for bringing it up again, but that's exactly what finally made me realize I needed to talk to you. The whole thing is just so erratic. Like, going from completely forgetting to eat all day to just tearing through whatever takeout or snacks I can find after midnight... it's just so back and forth. 

I'm really trying to get better at noticing when I should eat during the day, though. I hope I'm explaining this okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture so you don't think I'm doing this on purpose.
Do you feel like food is unappealing to you during the day?

Um, no, it's not that food is unappealing or gross to me or anything like that. I really don't want you to think I have some sort of aversion to food or an eating disorder. I actually really like food, usually! 

It's just... well, honestly, it's like I was saying before. I know I keep coming back to this, but it really is the main thing that scared me into coming in to see you. My eating has just been so all over the place. It's not that food is unappealing during the day, it's just that I completely forget meals because I'm so focused. And then, you know, the flip side is tearing through all those snacks and takeout after midnight. 

I'm really trying to do better, though. I'm trying to set alarms to remind myself to eat a normal lunch so I don't end up doing that at night. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way, I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the information you need.
Do you find yourself not wanting to eat during the day because you're just not interested in food at that time?

Um, yeah, I guess it's a lack of interest, but not in a bad way. I just... I get so wrapped up in my work that I don't really think about it. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or ignore my health. I know I should be eating more regularly. 

I feel like I keep repeating myself, and I'm so sorry if I'm not giving you what you're looking for, but... like I said, my eating has just been so all over the place. That's really the main thing that scared me into coming in. It's just... some days I forget meals completely, and then other nights I'm tearing through takeout and snacks after midnight. 

I'm really trying to get better at it, though. I want to be healthy. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
Do you usually feel hungry during the day when you're not eating?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel hungry. I really hope I'm not frustrating you by saying the same thing again... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. 

It's not that I'm feeling hunger pangs and just ignoring them. I would never do that, I know I need to take care of myself. It's just... like I mentioned before, my eating habits have just gotten so completely erratic. That's really the whole reason I'm here, it just got to a point where it scared me. Going from just totally forgetting to eat all day because I'm not feeling any hunger, to suddenly just... eating every snack in the house or ordering late-night takeout. It's just so back and forth. 

I'm really trying to get a handle on it, though. I'm trying to be more mindful. Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Do you feel like you're not eating during the day because you're simply not feeling hungry?

Um, yeah, I guess that's a good way to put it. I just... I don't really feel the hunger during the day. I'm so sorry, I feel terrible that I keep giving you the exact same answer over and over again. I really hope I'm not wasting your time or being difficult. 

It's just... like I was saying, it's honestly the main reason I finally made the appointment. My eating is just so all over the place right now, and it kind of freaked me out. Going from just completely forgetting to eat all day because I don't feel it, to suddenly tearing through takeout and whatever snacks I have around after midnight... it's just not like me. 

I'm really trying to fix it, though. I want to do the right thing and be healthy. Did I answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to figure this out.
Do you think you would eat during the day if you remembered to, or does the thought of eating during the day not appeal to you?

Um, I think if I remembered, I would try to eat. I really would. I wouldn't just refuse it if someone put a plate in front of me. I'm not trying to starve myself or anything, I promise. 

I know I'm sounding like a broken record here, and I'm so sorry, I just... I don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose. But like I've been saying, the whole reason I'm sitting here talking to you is because my eating has just gotten so completely out of whack. It really did scare me. It's just so bizarre to go from totally forgetting to eat a single thing all day long, to suddenly it's 1 AM and I'm just tearing through a massive takeout order and every snack in my pantry. 

I know it's not healthy, and I'm really trying to get better at finding a middle ground. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Is your lack of eating during the day more because you're not interested in food at that time or because you're too busy with other things to think about eating?

Um, I think it's more that I'm just... not interested in food during the day? Like, I'm busy, sure, but it's really just that the thought of eating doesn't even cross my mind. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself again, and I really don't want to be annoying or unhelpful. 

It's just that, honestly, this whole thing with my eating being so all over the place is the main reason I finally made myself come in. It really scared me, you know? Going from just completely forgetting to eat anything all day because I have zero interest in it, to suddenly it's late at night and I'm just tearing through takeout and whatever snacks I have... it's just so erratic. 

I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise. I want to have a normal routine. Did I answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you feel like you're not hungry at all during the day, or is it more that you're just not thinking about eating?

Um, I guess it's really that I'm just not thinking about it. Like my brain just completely skips over the idea of food entirely while the sun is up. 

Oh gosh, I'm so sorry, I know we're kind of stuck on this one thing and I feel awful if I'm not giving you the exact answer you're looking for. I promise I'm really trying. It's just... like I've been saying, that huge swing is what finally made me pick up the phone to see you. Going from literally forgetting that meals exist all day, to... well, the embarrassing part where I'm kind of out of control and eating all that takeout and junk food in the middle of the night. 

It's honestly a little shameful to admit how much I can put away at 2 AM, but it just scared me because it's so not how I usually am. I really hope that answers it a bit better? Please let me know if I need to clarify anything else, I just really want to make sure I'm doing this right and helping you out.
Do you think you would eat during the day if food was readily available and you were reminded to eat?

Um, yeah, I think so. If someone put it right in front of me and said, 'Hey, time to eat,' I would definitely try. I wouldn't just push it away. I'm really not trying to be difficult about it, I promise. 

I feel terrible because I know I keep circling back to this, and I hope you're not getting frustrated with me. I just... I want to be really clear because this whole food thing is honestly the main reason I finally made myself come see you. It's just so embarrassing to admit, but going from literally not having food cross my mind all day, to suddenly it's past midnight and I'm just inhaling an embarrassing amount of takeout and snacks... it just really freaked me out. It's so far from normal for me. 

I'm really trying to get a handle on it. Did that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me.
